senses.d: Having much distance in space from one end to the other.
ex: I need a long piece of wood.
It’s a long way from the Earth to the Moon.

senses.d: Specifically, having much distance in a horizontal dimension (see also Usage Notes below).
ex: This table is long but not very high.

senses.d: Travelling a great distance.
ex: Smith hoofs a long ball up to Jones.

senses.d: Having a long penis.
ex: My ex was very strong but not very long.

senses.d: Passing or landing ahead of or beyond the intended target or location.
ex: The plane touched down long and overran the end of the runway.

senses.d: Going beyond the intended target.
ex: That forehand was long. It landed two feet beyond the baseline.
The pass was long and was gathered by the opposing goalkeeper.

senses.d: Having great duration.
ex: His speech was long and dull.
The pyramids of Egypt have been around for a long time.

senses.d: Seeming to last a lot of time, due to being boring, tedious, tiring, irksome, etc.
ex: It took us three long weeks to clear the stones from the field.
It'll be a long journey home for the travelling supporters after that 5-0 defeat.

senses.d: Not short; tall.
ex: Bless ’em all, bless ’em all, the long, the short and the tall.

senses.d: Possessing or owning stocks, bonds, commodities, or other financial instruments with the aim of benefiting from an expected rise in their value.
ex: I’m long in DuPont.
I have a long position in DuPont.

senses.d: A long vowel.
ex: In French most vowels are half-long, and are only occasionally lengthened or shortened into full longs and shorts.

senses.d: A long syllable.
A note formerly used in music, one half the length of a large, twice that of a breve.
A long integer variable, twice the size of an int, two or four times the size of a short, and half of a long long.
ex: A long is typically 64 bits in a 32-bit environment.

senses.d: An entity with a long position in an asset; for example, a trader or investor possessing an amount of a company's shares.
ex: Every uptick made the longs cheer.

senses.d: A long-maturity security, such as a ten- or twenty-year bond.
To take a long position in.
ex: The left panel shows the profile of a portfolio consisting of longing a call and shorting a put.

senses.d: Over a great distance in space.
ex: Every golfer wants to hit the ball long and straight.

senses.d: Over too great a distance, beyond the target.
ex: She hit her return long and lost the point.

senses.d: For a particular duration (specified by additional qualifying words accompanying it).
ex: How long is it until the next bus arrives?
She has known us as long as you.

senses.d: For a long time.
ex: Paris has long been considered one of the most cultured cities in the world.
By eight o’clock, the food will be long gone.

senses.d: For a long time.
A long time (see usage notes).
ex: Will this interview take long?
I haven’t got long to live.

senses.d: A long time ago.
To await, aspire, desire greatly (something to occur or to be true).
ex: She longed for him to come back.

senses.d: On account of, because of.
To be appropriate to, to pertain or belong to.
ex: A goodly Armour, and full rich aray, / Which long’d to Angela, the Saxon Queene, / All fretted round with gold, and goodly wel beseene.
Tis well, and hold your owne in any case / With such austeritie as longeth to a father.

senses.d: To belong.
